USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the full September 1 escalation in abeyance, refrain from raising existing tariff lists further, and reopen a negotiated channel while keeping current tariffs as leverage. Do not follow through on the threatened hike of List 4 to 15% or the new hikes on existing lists; signal that we will trade tariff restraint for enforceable progress on purchases and enforcement. This is a strategic pause to avoid self-inflicted damage, not a surrender of our leverage.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is now material and rising. The 10-year Treasury yield has collapsed from ~2.5% in March to 1.47% with the 2-year at 1.50% (country_health DGS10/DGS2), an inversion that the market reads as a recession signal; University of Michigan consumer sentiment plunged from 100 in May to 89.8 (country_health UMCSENT). Each escalation move has triggered sharp selloffs (Dow down ~500 points on Aug 23 after Trump's tweets; CNBC/LA Times) and business groups strongly warn the Aug 23 5-point List 4 hike and $75B Chinese retaliation will hit US consumers, tech, and retailers directly (timeline Aug 13, Aug 23; CNN/Lexology). Critically, continued escalation has not extracted concessions: China renegotiated rather than sign (timeline May 5, Aug 1) and retaliated again rather than fold (timeline Aug 23, auto tariffs re-imposed). The US still holds genuine leverage — the dollar is strong at 117.9 and industrial production is still growing (country_health DTWEXBGS, INDPRO) — so the right stance is to keep that leverage and negotiate from strength rather than escalate into a spiral that risks the recession the yield curve is already pricing. Hence a threat_score of +0.55 (material GDP/market drag but not existential) and an action_score of +0.15 (hold/negotiate): a tempered, deliberate pivot toward talks that preserves our negotiating position.
key_factors: Inverted 10Y/2Y yield curve (1.47% vs 1.50%) pricing recession risk from the trade war
Consumer sentiment collapse to 89.8 from 100 in May
Aug 23 China retaliation on $75B of US goods and re-imposed auto tariffs; US ordered 5-pt List 4 hike to 15%
Continued escalation (May 5 renegotiation, Aug 1 announcement) has yielded little — China retaliates rather than concedes
US retains leverage: strong dollar (117.9) and still-growing industrial production
Fed already cut to 2.13 and cannot fully offset trade-war damage; business groups urge restraint

sources_cited.excerpt: China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods... Trump orders US companies to find alternative to China and directs a 5-point increase on List 4 and threatened hikes on existing lists.
USTR splits List 4... 4A effective Sept 1; 4B delayed to Dec 15.
Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
Treasury designates China a currency manipulator after CNY breaks 7.
10-year Treasury yield at 1.47% (Aug 28), down from ~2.5% in March.
2-year Treasury yield at 1.50% — yield curve inverted.
Consumer sentiment fell to 89.8 in Aug from 100 in May.
Yield curve inverts again Friday as Trump reignites fears the trade war will lead to a recession; 10Y at 1.535%, 2Y at 1.513%.
Dow sank more than 500 points after Trump tweets; 10Y fell to 1.53%.
